newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican labour union threatens a general strike.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican labour union threatens a general strike.

text.p: South Africa's largest labour movement Cosatu on Thursday threatened to begin mobilising its members for a general strike over a planned employment bill.
Cosatu has been in an uneasy alliance with the ruling African National Congress of President Nelson Mandela, but any mass action would be the most serious breach between the partners.
"We are mobilising our members because of the deadlock reached in terms of negotiations on the employment bill," a Cosatu spokeswoman told Reuters.
Cosatu has a total of 1.9 million members and plans a general strike on May 12.
Since it came to power in the country's first all-race elections in 1994, Mandela's government has confounded many of its right-wing critics by pursuing market-friendly policies.

But while the government's commitment to a free market and privatisation has wooed foreign investors and South Africa's still predominantly white business community, it has provoked argument with Cosatu and the South African Communist Party.

Cosatu said the main bones of contention with the planned law was a government-proposed 45-hour working week, while it wants a 40-hour maximum, and the length of paid maternity leave. There Cosatu wants a six-month paid period, while the government is offering four months paid leave.
